Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(ggmap)
library(leaflet)

API Key

register_stadiamaps("1ad11010-4c59-42b0-a160-0dab4e61577f", write = FALSE)

Load the Data

For this homework, we will use the shark attack data to visualize where the attacks occurred. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

sharks <- read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(longitude !="NA" & latitude !="NA") %>% # pulling out NA locations
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude)) # converting longitude to numeric
  1. Use the range of the latitude and longitude to build an appropriate bounding box for your map.
#get mins and maxes
sharks  %>%
  select(latitude, longitude) %>%
  summary()
##     latitude       longitude     
##  Min.   :32.59   Min.   :-124.7  
##  1st Qu.:34.04   1st Qu.:-123.1  
##  Median :36.70   Median :-122.0  
##  Mean   :36.36   Mean   :-121.4  
##  3rd Qu.:38.18   3rd Qu.:-119.6  
##  Max.   :41.56   Max.   :-117.1
#set latitude and longitude ranges, using min's & max's
lat <- c(32.59, 41.56)
long <- c(-124.7, -117.1)
#make bbox with 3% (f=0.03) buffer
bbox <- make_bbox(long, lat, f=0.03)
  1. Load a map from stamen in a terrain style projection and display the map.
map <- get_stadiamap(bbox, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom = 7)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
ggmap(map)

  1. Build a map that overlays the recorded observations of shark attacks in California.
ggmap(map)+
  geom_point(data=sharks, aes(longitude, latitude), size=0.5, color="black", alpha=0.6)+
  labs(x="Longitude", y="Latitude", title="CA: Shark Attacks, 1950-2022")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.2), hjust=0.5, face="bold"))

  1. Build a map that only shows the fatalities.
ggmap(map)+
  geom_point(data=sharks %>%
               filter(injury == "fatal"),
             aes(longitude, latitude), size=0.5, color="black", alpha=0.6)+
  labs(x="Longitude", y="Latitude", title="CA: Fatal Shark Attacks, 1950-2022")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.2), hjust=0.5, face="bold"))

  1. Build the same map (fatalities only), but this time make it interactive using leaflet. Also, color the points red.
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("x",
              "Select Variable of Interest:",
              choices = c("mode",
                          "depth",
                          "species"),
              selected = "mode"),
  plotOutput("plot",
             width = "500px",
             height = "800px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    sharks_fatal <- sharks %>%
      filter(injury == "fatal" & depth != "N/A")
    
    ggmap(map)+
      geom_point(data=sharks_fatal,
                 aes(x=longitude, y=latitude, shape=.data[[input$x]]),
                 size=2.5,
                 color="red",
                 alpha=0.7,
                 na.rm=T)+
      labs(x="Longitude", y="Latitude", title="CA: Fatal Shark Attacks, 1950-2022")+
      theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.8), hjust=0.5, face="bold"),
            axis.title.x=element_text(face="bold"),
            axis.title.y=element_text(face="bold"))
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
  1. Which county has the highest number of recorded shark attacks? Make a map that only shows the attacks in this county. (hint: it may help improve the map if you remove duplicate locations, i.e. multiple attacks at the same location.)
sharks %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  summarize(n_attacks = n()) %>%
  slice_max(n_attacks)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   county    n_attacks
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 San Diego        24
#San Diego has the most recorded shark attacks.
#get mins and maxes
sharks  %>%
  filter(county == "San Diego") %>%
  select(latitude, longitude) %>%
  summary()
##     latitude       longitude     
##  Min.   :32.59   Min.   :-118.1  
##  1st Qu.:32.77   1st Qu.:-117.6  
##  Median :32.85   Median :-117.4  
##  Mean   :32.97   Mean   :-117.5  
##  3rd Qu.:33.23   3rd Qu.:-117.3  
##  Max.   :33.37   Max.   :-117.1
#set latitude and longitude ranges, using min's & max's
lat_sd <- c(32.59, 33.37)
long_sd <- c(-118.1, -117.1)
#make bbox with 6% (f=0.06) buffer
bbox_sd <- make_bbox(long_sd, lat_sd, f=0.06)
#create map
map_sd <- get_stadiamap(bbox_sd, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom = 9)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
#plot map
ggmap(map_sd)+
  geom_point(data=sharks %>%
               filter(county == "San Diego"),
             aes(longitude, latitude), size=2, color="black", alpha=0.6)+
  labs(x="Longitude", y="Latitude", title="San Diego, CA: Shark Attacks, 1950-2022")
